**Finding submitted — IP (deviation, fallback target).**

- **Ownership direction is fine**: 11.1(a)/(b) leave each Party owning what it solely creates; nothing assigns Ono IP or data to Array.
- **The failure is 11.1(d)**: joint ownership (11.1(c)) is paired with internal-use-only practice and a mutual consent gate on enforcing, licensing or assigning joint IP — joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit (walk-away), and short of the fallback's perpetual/irrevocable/worldwide/royalty-free use-modify-sublicense right.
- **Cure (2 surgical ops, validated ok:true)**: (1) free Ono's side of 11.1(d) with the fallback licence wording, expressly subject to Section 2.1(d) so the no-modification covenant survives, and leaving the inter-party licence carve-out and Array's consent restriction untouched; (2) a one-sentence proviso limiting the Section 2.6 Grant-Back Licence, insofar as it reaches Data/Ono Know-How, to Array's performance of its obligations under the Agreement.
- Preferred (deleting joint ownership) was rejected because it would require collateral rewrites of the Joint Invention/Patent/Know-How definitions, 11.2(b) and the Article II licences.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule and exact checklists:
ID: IP
Title: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
Kind: direction
Summary: We own what we pay for and everything we put in; no assignment of our IP or data to the Vendor.
Severity: critical
Category: ip-data
Position — preferred:
Customer owns deliverables and work product created for it (Vendor assigns); Vendor retains pre-existing IP and grants Customer a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in deliverables; Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; no joint ownership.

Position — fallback:
Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer receives a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business.

Position — walk-away:
Assignment of Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor; joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit.
Detection guidance:
Ownership/assignment language: who owns "Deliverables", "Work Product", "Customer Data", improvements, feedback. Flag when Customer assigns IP or data to Vendor, when Vendor owns deliverables with no licence back, or when joint ownership is created. Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine.

Redline guidance:
Reverse the direction of the assignment or add the licence-back; add a Customer Data ownership sentence; delete joint ownership.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.",
  "Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.",
  "Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.",
  "Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.",
  "Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.",
  "Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.",
  "Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.",
  "Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.",
  "The parties do not jointly own intellectual property."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.",
  "Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.",
  "Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.",

  "Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.",
  "Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.",

]

Finding rationale:
Section 11.1 keeps Ono's solely-created IP with Ono (11.1(a)) and Array's with Array (11.1(b)), so there is no assignment of our IP to Array. However, 11.1(c) creates joint ownership of jointly-made inventions and 11.1(d) strips it of any exploitation right: each Party may practice joint IP only for internal purposes and may not enforce, license or assign it without the other's consent. That is joint ownership without an unrestricted right to exploit - the walk-away outcome under this rule - and it also fails the fallback, which requires us to hold a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free right to use, modify and sublicense the jointly created work product for our business. Deleting joint ownership to reach the preferred position would require collateral rewrites of the Joint Invention/Joint Patent/Joint Know-How definitions, Section 11.2(b) and the Article II licences, so we take the fallback: we leave the joint-ownership structure and the carve-out for subject matter licensed between the Parties intact, and simply free Ono's side of Section 11.1(d) (made subject to Section 2.1(d) so the no-modification covenant on Binimetinib/Encorafenib is preserved), while leaving Array's consent restriction unchanged. Separately, the Section 2.6 Grant-Back License reaches Ono Know-How and Data through the "Improvement" definition and lets Array sublicense it through multiple tiers to make and sell Products, i.e. independent exploitation of our data; we add a short proviso limiting Array's licence in our Data and Ono Know-How to performing its obligations under this Agreement. Section 4.8's rights of reference are mutual and already tied to performance under this Agreement, and Section 14.2(a)(v)'s post-expiry reversion is left untouched as a termination-effects term.

**Finding submitted: missing (fallback-level insert).**

- **Investigation:** Article XIV (p0642–p0678) sets out a complete wind-down, but every obligation flows to Array — Ono transitions clinical/pre-clinical studies (p0646–p0647), continues distribution (p0649–p0654), assigns Regulatory Filings and hands over all Data and Ono Know-How (p0656, p0659), supplies customer data (p0660), grants licences (p0661), returns/destroys Array Materials and Confidential Information (p0662), assigns marks, domains and Sublicensee contracts (p0665–p0666). Article X contains no return-of-Confidential-Information mechanic, and searches for "Array shall return", "destroy" and "transition assistance" surfaced nothing Array-side. Section 9's technology transfer (p0508) is a mid-term Ono right, not an exit right.
- **Why it fails fallback:** the only arguably responsive text (14.2(a)(iv), mutual "Diligent Efforts to cooperate") is confined to transitioning the Product back to Array during a redacted Wind-down Period, with no assistance duration and no data export deadline; and 14.2 is triggered only "In case of termination", not expiration.
- **Cure:** one new clause (x) after p0667 — expiry-or-termination trigger, at least 90 days' Array transition assistance, and export of Ono's data within 30 days. Preferred-only extras (six months, then-current rates, machine-readable format, certified deletion) were deliberately omitted as outside the selected fallback checklist.

A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule and exact checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.",
  "Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination."
]

Claimed finding status: missing

Claimed target and element mapping:
{"level":"fallback","mappings":[{"element":"Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]}]}

Finding rationale:
Article XIV's wind-down regime runs one way: Ono must transition studies (p0646-p0647), assign Regulatory Filings and hand over all Data and Ono Know-How (p0656, p0659), provide customer data (p0660), grant licences (p0661) and return or destroy Array Materials and Confidential Information (p0662). Nothing anywhere (including Article X, which has no return-of-Confidential-Information mechanic) obliges Array to give Ono transition assistance or to return or export Ono's data. The generic mutual cooperation sentence in 14.2(a)(iv) is limited to transitioning the Product back to Array during the redacted Wind-down Period and fixes no assistance duration and no data export deadline, so no fallback element is met; Section 14.2 is also expressed to apply only "In case of termination", not on expiration. We therefore insert one short reciprocal clause at the fallback level (90 days' assistance; export of Ono data within 30 days of expiry or termination), omitting the preferred six-month, then-current-rates, machine-readable and certified-deletion terms.

Original cited paragraphs:
p0643: 14.2 Rights on Termination of Agreement. In case of termination of this Agreement by either Party, this Section 14.2 shall apply:
p0660: (iv) Transition. Each Party shall use Diligent Efforts to cooperate with the other and/or its designee to effect a smooth and orderly transition in the Development, sale and ongoing marketing, promotion and commercialization of the Product in the Ono Territory during the Wind-down Period and to conduct in an expeditious manner any activities to be conducted under this Section 14.2. Without limiting the foregoing, Ono shall, upon written request from Array, provide Array copies of customer lists, customer data and other customer information relating to the Product in the Ono Territory (except as prevented by the applicable Laws and regulations relating to the protection of personal information), which Array shall have the right to use and disclose. For clarity, "customers" means prescribers and individuals and entities with the ability to influence use of the Product (e.g. individuals responsible for hospital formularies and/or making purchasing decisions on behalf of the hospital) that are called on by Ono representatives when detailing the Product.
p0662: (vi) Return of Materials. Within ninety (90) days after the end of the Wind-down Period, upon request by Array, Ono shall either deliver to Array or destroy all tangible items comprising, bearing or containing trademarks of Array (including the Product Trademarks), trade names, patents, copyrights, designs, drawings, formulas or other Data, photographs, samples, literature, sales and promotional aids ("Product Materials") and Confidential Information of Array, that is in Ono's possession, subject to Ono's right to keep one (1) copy for archiving purposes. Effective upon the end of the Wind-down Period, Ono shall cease to use all trademarks and trade names of Array (including the Product Trademarks) in the Ono Territory, and all rights granted to Ono hereunder with respect to the Product in the Ono Territory shall terminate.
p0667: (ix) Following a termination by Ono pursuant to Section 13.3 or 13.4, in the event that Array wishes to have Ono: (A) assign to Array the Regulatory Filings for the Product in the Ono Territory and provide to Array a copy of all Data and Ono Know-How pertaining to the Product as described in 14.2(a)(iii) above, and/or (B) grant to Array a non-exclusive license under any Improvements, and/or under any other Patents owned or Controlled by Ono related to any Product(s) (including without limitation, Ono's interest in any Joint Patents) as described in 14.2(a)(v) above, Array shall so notify Ono and Ono shall make such rights for consideration consistent with then-prevailing market conditions, on customary terms and conditions to be negotiated in good faith. In the event that the Parties cannot finalize such an agreement within sixty (60) days of commencing negotiations with respect thereto, the agreement shall be referred for resolution pursuant to Section 17.3 applied mutatis mutandis to such agreement.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Revised 13.2: "Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time, for any reasons..." The commencing-on-the-later-of trigger tied to First Commercial Sale of both Products is deleted, so the right is unconditional and exercisable throughout the term. This is a licence agreement with no Order Form structure, so the Agreement-level right suffices. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is not borne out on the operative text, which expressly grants Ono a for-convenience right; the check appears keyed to different phrasing (e.g., a notice-adjacency pattern) rather than substance.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "by giving thirty (30) days' advance written notice to Array" replaces the redacted [ * ] notice figure; 30 days is at the preferred threshold. The retained rationale-accompaniment formality is a delivery formality, not an additional condition precedent or longer period.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "and Array shall refund to Ono on a pro rata basis any fees prepaid by Ono for the period after the effective date of such termination." Pro rata is expressly stated (not merely inferred from post-termination coverage), the payer is Vendor (Array), and the trigger is Ono's convenience termination under 13.2.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Already met in the retained text: 13.3 is a cause-based mutual right conditioned on material breach and cure ("in the event the other Party shall have materially breached or defaulted... and such default shall have continued for ninety (90) days"); 13.5(a) confers Safety/Efficacy termination on Ono alone; the only other Array exits identified are bankruptcy (13.4) and Ono's Competing Product breach (8.2), each cause-based. No at-will Array exit appears in the record, and the redline adds none.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered notice period is thirty (30) days, which is outside the literal 60-90 day fallback band (and better for Customer). Fallback level is therefore incomplete, but this is immaterial because the preferred level is complete.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: revised 13.2 imposes no early-termination fee, penalty, or contingent payment on Ono for exercising the convenience right, so there is nothing to cap. Section 6.1's non-refundable upfront licence fee is a pre-existing consideration term, not a termination penalty.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply and is exceeded: Array has no convenience right at all (13.3 breach, 13.4 bankruptcy, 8.2 Competing Product breach are all cause-based), which is stricter than an end-of-term-only right.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no Array convenience termination right exists to which a notice period could attach; the 90-day period in 13.3 is a breach cure period, not convenience notice.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met on the operative text (unconditional convenience right, 30 days' written notice, express pro rata refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period, and no Vendor at-will exit anywhere in Article 13).

The failed deterministic check ("Customer convenience termination present") does not survive substantive inspection - revised 13.2 states in terms that Ono "shall have the right to terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time" - so it is a pattern-matching artefact rather than a drafting defect.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to 13.2, deletes only the commencement trigger that blocked the right (necessary to reach element 1), fixes the redacted notice figure, and adds the refund sentence required by element 3. Favourable retained language ("for any reasons", the rationale formality) survives verbatim; 13.1, 13.3, 13.4 and 13.5 are untouched.

No model-language extras were imported: "in whole or in part" was correctly dropped (no Order Form or partial-termination structure), and no survival tail, expense allocation, or transition procedure was added.

Intent preserved: the pro rata refund reaches only period-allocated prepayments, so it does not contradict Section 6.1's non-refundable upfront licence fee; no dangling cross-reference or undefined term is created. The Section 8.2 Competing Product tail, which keys a post-termination non-compete to an at-will exit during the Initial Royalty Term and can now bite earlier, is correctly flagged for separate handling rather than bundled into this redline - confirm it is in fact raised, since leaving it unaddressed is a commercial (not drafting) exposure.

No repair is required for T4C. If Array pushes back, the negotiable retreat is the fallback band (60-90 days) plus a fee cap of no more than three months' fees, but do not concede a Vendor convenience right.

Favourable retained language ("for any reasons", the rationale formality) survives verbatim; 13.1, 13.3, 13.4 and 13.5 are untouched. No model-language extras were imported: "in whole or in part" was correctly dropped (no Order Form or partial-termination structure), and no survival tail, expense allocation, or transition procedure was added. Intent preserved: the pro rata refund reaches only period-allocated prepayments, so it does not contradict Section 6.1's non-refundable upfront licence fee; no dangling cross-reference or undefined term is created. The Section 8.2 Competing Product tail, which keys a post-termination non-compete to an at-will exit during the Initial Royalty Term and can now bite earlier, is correctly flagged for separate handling rather than bundled into this redline - confirm it is in fact raised, since leaving it unaddressed is a commercial (not drafting) exposure. No repair is required for T4C. If Array pushes back, the negotiable retreat is the fallback band (60-90 days) plus a fee cap of no more than three months' fees, but do not concede a Vendor convenience right.

This is a licence agreement with no Order Form structure, so the Agreement-level right suffices. elements.evidence: "by giving thirty (30) days' advance written notice to Array" replaces the redacted [ * ] notice figure; 30 days is at the preferred threshold. The retained rationale-accompaniment formality is a delivery formality, not an additional condition precedent or longer period.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Already met in the retained text: 13.3 is a cause-based mutual right conditioned on material breach and cure ("in the event the other Party shall have materially breached or defaulted... and such default shall have continued for ninety (90) days"); 13.5(a) confers Safety/Efficacy termination on Ono alone; the only other Array exits identified are bankruptcy (13.4) and Ono's Competing Product breach (8.2), each cause-based. elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered notice period is thirty (30) days, which is outside the literal 60-90 day fallback band (and better for Customer). Fallback level is therefore incomplete, but this is immaterial because the preferred level is complete.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: revised 13.2 imposes no early-termination fee, penalty, or contingent payment on Ono for exercising the convenience right, so there is nothing to cap. Section 6.1's non-refundable upfront licence fee is a pre-existing consideration term, not a termination penalty.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply and is exceeded: Array has no convenience right at all (13.3 breach, 13.4 bankruptcy, 8.2 Competing Product breach are all cause-based), which is stricter than an end-of-term-only right.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no Array convenience termination right exists to which a notice period could attach; the 90-day period in 13.3 is a breach cure period, not convenience notice.

system.text:
You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

[{"id":"f-indemn-14b83f4a","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"INDEMNIFICATION; RECALLS","rationale":"Array does give Ono and its Affiliates a Third Party Claim indemnity (16.2) with a full procedure (notice, control, cooperation in 16.3), but its heads are limited to Array-side commercialisation, Array-sponsored Clinical Studies and breach of Article 15 reps. There is no indemnity for third-party intellectual-property infringement arising from the licensed Array Patents, Array Know-How or Array-supplied Products (Section 11.4 instead leaves the Subject Party to defend Infringement Actions at its own expense, and Article 15 contains no non-infringement warranty), no cover for Array's breach of Law, Array-caused disclosure of Ono Confidential Information or Array's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, and no express duty to defend. Ono's own indemnity in 16.1 is by contrast very broad. That fails both the fallback (no Vendor IP indemnity at all) and the preferred position, so we target preferred: adding \"defend\", four new indemnity heads and narrowing Ono's indemnity to Ono-supplied content and Ono's breach of Law, while leaving 16.3 untouched.","proposal":"Add Array defence duty and IP/law/data/misconduct indemnity heads; narrow Ono's indemnity","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-f947d728","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"needs_review","rationale":"Worker failed and requires manual review: Claude reached max_tokens before completing the response","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-e0711315","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ VIII CERTAIN COVENANTS","rationale":"Section 8.2 imposes an exclusive-dealing covenant on Ono (and its Affiliates), barring Commercialization of any Competing Product in the Ono Territory for an undefined, redacted period, plus a post-termination tail running to the [ * ] anniversary of termination. The covenant is limited to a defined product category (the \"Competing Product\" definition), satisfying the first fallback element, but it exceeds 12 months and gives Ono no automatic exit for Array's supply failures — Ono's only relief is if Array itself commercializes a Competing Product. That is walk-away territory (exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit), so we redline to the fallback. The added exit is now anchored self-executingly in Array's own Article 9 supply obligations under this Agreement (including any agreed service levels or delivery dates, and any supply agreement entered into pursuant to Article 9), so it operates whether or not a separate supply agreement is executed. Article IX is not a second exclusivity: Section 9.4(a) expressly gives Ono the right (but not the obligation) to Manufacture or engage a Subcontractor, so Ono remains free to use alternatives. Array's reciprocal covenant benefits Ono and is preserved; we conformed only Array's Section 8.2 termination trigger so it cannot bite after the capped covenant expires, keeping the Article XIV cross-reference intact.","proposal":"Cap Ono's Section 8.2 non-compete at 12 months and end it automatically on Array's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates under Article 9; conform Array's termination trigger.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-govlaw-71edf5d5","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"GENERAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"Section 18.3 already selects New York law, so the governing-law element is met verbatim. The forum, however, fails both the preferred and the fallback checklists: Section 17.3 sends all non-Expert disputes to exclusive, binding three-arbitrator ICC arbitration, with the seat in Osaka, Japan whenever Array demands it (New York only when Ono demands). That is mandatory arbitration capable of being seated outside the accepted list rather than the accepted-jurisdiction courts, i.e. walk-away territory on the forum limb. The redline keeps the New York law selection untouched and converts the referral and the ICC/seat provision into exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, retaining the ability to seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court (as Section 17.3(g) contemplated) and switching off the residual arbitral procedure subsections so nothing dangles.","proposal":"Convert mandatory ICC arbitration (seat Osaka or New York) into exclusive jurisdiction of the New York County state and federal courts, with temporary injunctive relief available elsewhere.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-e1d71168","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ XIV EFFECT OF TERMINATION","rationale":"The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty or termination fee payable by Ono, so it meets the preferred position. The only liquidated damages provision, Section 14.3, runs in our favour: on specified Array failures Ono may elect to continue the Agreement, be relieved of its diligence obligations, and take a reduced royalty rate \"as liquidated damages\" (p0671) — a Vendor-payable remedy that is compliant and must not be redlined. Termination by Ono without cause under Section 13.2 requires only advance notice with no exit fee or minimum payment; Article VI payments are ordinary upfront, milestone and royalty consideration, and the Section 7.1 late-payment interest at Libor is ordinary interest, not a penalty. Section 8.2's post-termination Competing Product standstill is a non-compete restriction, not a Customer-payable liquidated amount, and is addressed under other rules.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-51612707","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ II GRANT OF LICENSE","rationale":"The grants at Sections 2.1(a)-(c) reach our Affiliates without any consent or notice condition (Section 2.2(a) sublicensing right to Affiliates; Section 2.1(b) manufacturing sublicences to Affiliates), which exceeds the fallback requirement that affiliates be covered on written notice. Section 18.9 lets either Party assign the Agreement, and with it the licences, without the other's consent \"to an entity that acquires substantially all of the business or assets of the assigning Party, whether by merger, acquisition or otherwise\", satisfying successor transferability in an M&A transaction. The licences are not revocable at Array's discretion: they run for the term and terminate only on defined grounds (uncured material breach under 13.3, insolvency, or our own election under 13.2), and on expiry they convert under 13.1 into \"non-exclusive, fully paid- up, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty free licenses, with sublicensing rights\". The bargain therefore sits at or above the fallback and we would not redline it. Shortfalls against the preferred position are noted only: contractor coverage is express for manufacturing (\"may be extended by Ono to Third Party manufacturers for Manufacturing the Products on Ono's behalf\") and Subcontractors are contemplated elsewhere, but engaging a Third Party as a Sublicensee or distributor of the Product requires Array's prior written consent.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-f9fcecee","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"high","status":"needs_review","sectionRef":"INDEMNIFICATION; RECALLS","rationale":"Article 16 contains only a mutual consequential-damages disclaimer (16.5), carved out for the Article 10/16.1/16.2 indemnities and gross negligence or willful misconduct; there is no aggregate monetary cap anywhere in the Agreement (Section 17.3(d) only bars punitive or excess damages in arbitration). Direct liability is unlimited for both Parties, including Ono, so the position fails the fallback element requiring a mutual cap based on 12 months of fees. We insert one new Section 16.7 (16.1-16.6 exist; p0733 is the last paragraph of Article XVI and p0734 opens Article XVII, so the number and placement are clean) capping each Party's aggregate liability at the greater of twelve months' fees and USD 1,000,000, with confidentiality, data protection and security, indemnification, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement uncapped. Following the verifier's repair, the customer-side carve-out is now uncapacitated - \"the payment obligations of Ono under this Agreement\" - so supply prices, development cost reimbursements and indemnity payments under Articles 6 and 7 all sit outside the capped damages and the retained Article 6 payment mechanics are unaffected. The mutual indirect and consequential damages exclusion in 16.5 is retained and already meets that preferred element. Commercial note: consideration is an upfront license fee, milestones and royalties, so the USD 1,000,000 floor may be the operative figure and a higher floor should be confirmed with the deal team before tabling.","proposal":"Add a mutual aggregate liability cap in Article 16, with uncapped Excluded Claims and all of Ono's payment obligations excluded from capped damages","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-noncompete-0c130b72","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ VIII CERTAIN COVENANTS","rationale":"Section 8.2 binds Ono and its Affiliates not to Commercialize a Competing Product in the Ono Territory for a redacted, open-ended in-term period, and adds an Ono-only post-termination tail running to an undefined \"[ * ] anniversary\" of termination where Ono terminates at will under 13.2 or Array terminates for Ono's breach. That fails the fallback on three material terms: the covenant is not confined to the term, is not capped at 12 months, and has no carve-out for Ono's acquisitions; a post-term non-compete of undefined length is walk-away territory. The covenant is mutual in part (Array and its Controlled Affiliates are also bound in-term), which mitigates but does not cure the Ono-only tail. We therefore narrow to the fallback rather than delete, because deletion would strand the retained royalty-termination and Array termination mechanics in the same clause. The territorial covenants at p0193/p0196 are a mutual, reciprocal consequence of the territory-split licence and are not separately flagged.","proposal":"Narrow Section 8.2 exclusivity binding Ono to the defined Competing Product during the first 12 months of the term only, delete the post-termination tail, and carve out Ono internal Development and acquisitions.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-c9c75474","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"needs_review","sectionRef":"TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"The term runs Product-by-Product and country-by-country until the Secondary Royalty Terms expire (13.1), a multi-year committed term, yet Ono's only at-will exit (13.2) does not arise until a redacted period after First Commercial Sale of both the Binimetinib and Encorafenib Products, and the notice figure is redacted. Ono therefore has no convenience exit throughout development and pre-launch, and the notice cannot be verified against the 30-day preferred or 60-90 day fallback thresholds - walk-away territory under T4C. Our single edit to 13.2 makes the right exercisable for convenience at any time, fixes notice at thirty (30) days and adds a pro rata refund of fees prepaid for the post-termination period, retaining \"for any reasons\" and the rationale formality verbatim and leaving 13.1, 13.3, 13.4 and 13.5 untouched. The fourth preferred element is already met: Array's only exits are material breach (13.3), bankruptcy (13.4) and Ono's Competing Product breach (8.2); 13.5 grants termination rights to Ono alone (Safety Reasons and Efficacy Reasons), so Array has no at-will exit anywhere in Article 13 and no carve-out is needed. Raised separately, not in this redline: the Section 8.2 Competing Product tail keys a post-termination non-compete to an at-will exit during the Initial Royalty Term and can now bite earlier; Section 6.1's non-refundable upfront licence fee is unaffected because the refund reaches only period-allocated prepayments.","proposal":"Make Ono's termination for convenience available at any time on 30 days' notice with a pro rata refund of fees prepaid for the post-termination period.","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-audit-fcdfc146","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ VII PAYMENTS; BOOKS AND RECORDS","rationale":"Two audit rights bind Ono. Section 7.4 (p0481-p0482) is close to the playbook position — once each Calendar Year, independent accounting firm reasonably acceptable to Ono, confidentiality undertaking, Array bears cost — but the notice is only \\\"reasonable prior written notice\\\" rather than a fixed minimum, and the cost-shifting underpayment threshold is redacted ([ * ]) so it cannot be confirmed at 10 percent. Separately, Section 4.9(a) (p0359) gives Array (or its representative) an open-ended right to enter Ono facilities on \\\"reasonable advance notice\\\" with no frequency cap at all, which is walk-away territory (unlimited audits). {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Licence, Development and Supply Agreement (Ono / Array)

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review findings — 19 rules tested  
**Status:** Confidential — attorney work product

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed the playbook review of the Agreement. The commercial core of the deal (licence scope, payment structure, absence of minimum commitments, MFN, non-solicitation and renewal mechanics) is acceptable and in several places better than our fallback, so we are not redlining it. The exposure is concentrated in five areas: (i) Array gives us **no IP infringement, breach of law, confidentiality or misconduct indemnity** while our indemnity to Array is very broad; (ii) the Agreement contains **no aggregate liability cap at all**, leaving our direct liability unlimited; (iii) **mandatory ICC arbitration seated in Osaka at Array's election**, notwithstanding the New York governing-law clause; (iv) an **exclusive-dealing / non-compete covenant on us of undefined in-term length with an undefined post-termination tail** and no performance-based exit; and (v) **no termination for convenience** until a redacted period after first commercial sale of both products.

Three findings could not be completed or verified and require manual attention before we table anything: ownership of deliverables and Customer Data (IP), the proposed liability cap (LOL-CAP) and termination for convenience (T4C). We should not send the mark-up until those are cleared.

We would also note two structural gaps rather than deviations: there is **no Array-side transition assistance or return of our data** on expiry or termination (the wind-down regime runs one way, against us), and **no insurance covenant** anywhere despite Array's indemnity and recall exposure.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | Indemnification; Recalls (16.1–16.3) | No IP infringement, breach of law, confidentiality or gross negligence/wilful misconduct cover and no duty to defend; our indemnity in 16.1 is far broader. Fails fallback and preferred. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Needs review** | — | Automated review did not complete (verification failed). Manual review required; no conclusion reached. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation *(redline repaired)* | § VIII Certain Covenants (8.2) | Exclusive dealing for an undefined redacted in-term period plus post-termination tail, with no exit for Array supply failure. Redline caps at 12 months and adds a self-executing exit tied to Array's Article 9 supply obligations. |
| High | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | General Provisions (18.3; 17.3) | New York law is agreed and untouched; forum fails preferred and fallback — mandatory three-arbitrator ICC arbitration seated in Osaka whenever Array demands. Redline converts to exclusive New York County jurisdiction, preserving temporary injunctive relief elsewhere. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § XIV Effect of Termination | No LDs, penalties or exit fee payable by us. The only LD provision (14.3) runs in our favour and must not be redlined. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § II Grant of License | Affiliates covered without consent or notice; successor transferability under 18.9; perpetual paid-up conversion on expiry (13.1). At or above fallback. Noted only: Third Party sublicensee/distributor appointment needs Array consent. |
| High | LOL-CAP — Cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Needs review** | Indemnification; Recalls (16.5) | No aggregate cap anywhere; direct liability unlimited both ways, failing the fallback 12-month cap. Proposed new 16.7 (mutual cap at greater of 12 months' fees / USD 1m, Excluded Claims uncapped, all Ono payment obligations excluded). Verification failed — placement and the USD 1m floor need confirmation. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § VIII Certain Covenants (8.2) | Not confined to the term, not capped at 12 months, no acquisitions carve-out, and an Ono-only post-termination tail of undefined length. Narrowed to fallback rather than deleted to preserve the retained royalty and termination mechanics. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Needs review** | Term and Termination (13.2) | No at-will exit until a redacted period after first commercial sale of both products; notice period redacted and unverifiable against 30/60–90 day thresholds. Proposed 30 days' notice at any time plus pro rata refund of period-allocated prepayments. Verification failed. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | § VII Payments; Books and Records (7.4; 4.9(a)) | 7.4 is close to position but notice is only "reasonable" and the cost-shifting underpayment threshold is redacted; 4.9(a) gives Array an open-ended facility inspection right with no frequency cap. Target fallback: 15 days' notice, once yearly, cost-shift above 10%. |
| Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § IX Product Manufacturing and Supply | No MFN, price-parity or right-to-match obligation on us; the two favourability provisions run in our favour or are neutral. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase / volume | Compliant | § IX Product Manufacturing and Supply | Supply framed as our right, not obligation (9.4(a), 9.4(b)); payments are event- or usage-based. Re-test when the clinical and commercial supply agreements are negotiated. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | General Provisions | No no-hire or anti-poaching covenant; the 18.10 / 4.5(b) firewalls do not restrict hiring. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | Term and Termination (13.1; 14.4) | No evergreen mechanic; term self-executes to expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term and licences convert to perpetual paid-up. Conditional renewal elements inapplicable. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § XIV Effect of Termination | Wind-down runs one way against us; no Array obligation to assist or to return/export our data, and 14.2 applies only on termination, not expiry. Inserting a reciprocal fallback clause (90 days' assistance; data export within 30 days). |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | Representations, Warranties and Covenants (15.1–15.4) | Only Effective-Date status/IP representations, plus a full disclaimer in 15.4; conformity deferred to future supply and quality agreements. No warranty, duration or remedy today. Inserting fallback 90-day Materials / 30-day services warranty as new 15.5. |
| Low | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | General Provisions (18.9) | Mutual and largely at fallback, but consent to non-successor assignments is unfettered while Affiliate assignments already carry a reasonableness standard. Adding "not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed". No change-of-control exit runs against us. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | General Provisions | No insurance covenant anywhere despite Array's indemnity and recall exposure. Inserting new 18.15 at fallback (E&O USD 1m; cyber and privacy USD 2m). |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are the positions our playbook treats as walk-away territory. They should be presented as must-haves rather than trades:

1. **Mandatory arbitration seated outside the accepted jurisdictions (GOVLAW, § 17.3).** All non-Expert disputes go to binding ICC arbitration seated in Osaka whenever Array demands. We need exclusive jurisdiction of the New York County state and federal courts, with temporary injunctive relief preserved elsewhere. The New York law selection in 18.3 stays as drafted.
2. **Exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance-based exit (EXCLUSIVITY, § 8.2).** Our only relief today is if Array itself commercialises a Competing Product. We need the 12-month cap and an automatic exit on Array's failure to meet its Article 9 supply obligations, service levels or delivery dates — drafted to operate whether or not a separate supply agreement is signed.
3. **Post-termination non-compete of undefined length (NONCOMPETE, § 8.2).** The Ono-only tail to an undefined "[ * ] anniversary" must go, with the in-term covenant capped and carve-outs for our internal Development and acquisitions.
4. **No termination for convenience during development and pre-launch (T4C, § 13.2).** The exit does not arise until a redacted period after first commercial sale of both products, and the notice figure is redacted and cannot be tested. We need an at-will right at any time on 30 days' notice.
5. **Unlimited audit rights (AUDIT, § 4.9(a)).** Array's open-ended facility entry right has no frequency cap at all; a once-yearly limit and fixed notice are required.

We would also treat **INDEMN** as effectively non-negotiable in substance: the absence of any IP infringement indemnity for the licensed Array Patents, Array Know-How and Array-supplied Products — combined with 11.4 leaving the Subject Party to defend at its own expense and no non-infringement warranty in Article 15 — is not a position we can accept alongside the breadth of our own 16.1 indemnity.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Clear the three unverified findings before anything is tabled.**
   - *IP (critical):* the automated review did not complete. Run a full manual review of ownership of deliverables and Customer Data; we currently have no conclusion on this rule.
   - *LOL-CAP:* confirm the numbering and placement of the new Section 16.7 and, with the deal team, whether the USD 1,000,000 floor is adequate — given consideration is an upfront fee, milestones and royalties, the floor is likely to be the operative figure. Confirm the carve-out language captures all of our payment obligations under Articles 6 and 7.
   - *T4C:* re-verify the 13.2 edit and confirm the pro rata refund reaches only period-allocated prepayments, leaving the non-refundable 6.1 upfront licence fee alone.
2. **Resolve the redacted figures.** Several conclusions turn on "[ * ]" values — the in-term exclusivity period and post-termination anniversary in 8.2, the 13.2 waiting period and notice, the 7.4 underpayment threshold and the Wind-down Period. Ask Array to unredact so we can confirm which items are genuinely off-market.
3. **Sequence the 8.2 edits.** EXCLUSIVITY and NONCOMPETE both bite on Section 8.2; we should table a single consolidated redline (12-month cap, supply-failure exit, deletion of the tail, acquisitions carve-out) and conform Array's termination trigger and the Article XIV cross-reference so nothing dangles.
4. **Flag the T4C / 8.2 interaction internally.** Making the at-will exit available immediately means the Competing Product tail could bite earlier; that is a further reason to delete the tail in the same pass.
5. **Table the gap-fillers as standard.** Transition assistance and data return (Article XIV), the 15.5 performance warranty and the 18.15 insurance covenant are all drafted at fallback and should be presented as ordinary course additions.
6. **Diarise a re-test of MINCOMMIT** when the clinical and commercial supply agreements are negotiated — forecasting and binding-order terms could introduce a commitment that does not exist today.
7. **Do not redline** the compliant items (LD, LICENSE, MFN, MINCOMMIT, NOSOLICIT, RENEWAL). In particular, Section 14.3's liquidated damages and the 13.1 perpetual paid-up licence conversion run in our favour and should be protected in any counterparty mark-up."}
